Lessons.Title: Use Equivalent Fractions to Compare
ExplanationParagraphs: Grade4 Unit2 Lesson13 First Edition2021: compare fractions by rewriting one as an equivalent fraction with SAME denominator when one denominator divides the other. Preserve learning goals, academic standards and existing correct intro.

Warm-up Notice and Wonder Pairs of Numbers10min: four ORIGINAL statements are5<8 true;9/2>4 1/2 false, actually equal;4=3/2 false;1/3<1/2 true. Students read inequality symbols aloud and explain each judgement.

Activity1 Pairs to Compare20min: six source pairs organized by benchmark grouping. Group1 (both<1/2):2/10 versus26/100, choose26/100;2/5 versus11/100, choose2/5. Group2 (both between1/2 and1):2/3 versus7/12, choose2/3;4/5 versus7/10, choose4/5. Group3 (both>1):11/5 versus26/10, choose26/10;11/3 versus26/12, choose11/3. Explain by exact equivalent denominator or benchmarks.

Activity2 New Pairs to Compare15min: evaluate source assertions5/12=2/6 false;10/3<44/12 true;1/4>25/100 false because equal;8/15<3/5 true. Complete six original pairs with relational symbols<,>,<,<,>,< respectively for6/12 vs4/6;4/3 vs7/6;8/5 vs400/100;12/10 vs35/5;11/4 vs17/8;7/12 vs4/3. Use exact rational comparisons.

Lesson synthesis10min: compare fractions by common denominator and alternative model/benchmarks; source classroom reasoning and partner discussions are teacher-reviewed, while existing exact Practice only covers numerical decisions.

Edulytics original five-minute Cool-down (not source publisher original protected task): explain why2/3>7/12 and why1/4=25/100 using corresponding common-denominator fractions. Teacher reviews verbal or drawn proofs.

KeyConcepts.Title: Common denominator strategy
KeyConcepts.Definition: Express two fractions in equal-size fractional units.

KeyConcepts.Title: Fraction inequality
KeyConcepts.Definition: Use <,=,> according to exact rational sizes.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Do not infer direction from denominator digits.

KeyConcepts.Title: Benchmarks
KeyConcepts.Definition: Use0,1/2,1 to classify before refining within a class.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Two fractions both above1 may still differ in size.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Classifying two fractions in the same benchmark group as automatically equal.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Relative to1/2 or1 is insufficient for their order.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use common denominators or another exact argument.

SummaryPoints: Original 2021 Student Task Statements PDF3p and teacher source read.
Four warm-up claims, six grouped pairs, four source true/false and six inequality completions accurately included.
Use shared denominators when one is multiple of the other; teacher also accepts valid benchmark strategies.
Independent first-party goal-aligned Cool-down is teacher-reviewed, protected publisher original not claimed.
